message.content:
Using the formula for the sum of sines in arithmetic progression,
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{n}\sin(kx)=\frac{\sin\left(\frac{nx}{2}\right)\sin\left(\frac{(n+1)x}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)}.
\]
Here \(n=35\) and \(x=5^\circ\), so
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{35}\sin(5k)^\circ
=
\frac{\sin\left(\frac{35\cdot 5^\circ}{2}\right)\sin\left(\frac{36\cdot 5^\circ}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\frac{5^\circ}{2}\right)}.
\]
This becomes
\[
\frac{\sin(87.5^\circ)\sin(90^\circ)}{\sin(2.5^\circ)}
=
\frac{\sin(87.5^\circ)}{\sin(2.5^\circ)}.
\]
Since \(\sin(87.5^\circ)=\cos(2.5^\circ)\),
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{35}\sin(5k)^\circ
=
\frac{\cos(2.5^\circ)}{\sin(2.5^\circ)}
=
\cot(2.5^\circ).
\]
But
\[
\cot(2.5^\circ)=\tan(90^\circ-2.5^\circ)=\tan(87.5^\circ).
\]
Thus
\[
\tan(r^\circ)=\tan(87.5^\circ),
\]
so
\[
r=87.5^\circ+180^\circ n.
\]
The smallest positive rational value is
\[
r=87.5=\frac{175}{2}.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\frac{175}{2}}\).
